question.text: Under Series XIX-A (Category I and II AIF) due diligence, which of the following risk-related items is the workbook MOST likely to ask a distributor to evaluate?

answer.text: The number of stocks in the long book only
Exposure limits to a single investee company, the fund's leverage policy, and the PPM's general risk factors

explanation.text: The Logic: The Series XIX-A workbook directs distributors to check exposure limits to a single investee company, review the fund's leverage policy, and study the general risk factors disclosed in the PPM. The workbook also states that hedge-fund / Category III long-short discussion is outside its scope, so DD prompts here stay within Category I/II risk and exposure language. The Trap: Dividend yield is not a Category I/II risk metric, counting only long positions is meaningless for a Category I/II fund, and office rental cost is an operational item, not an investment risk. Note: Category III hedge-fund metrics like net/gross exposure and maximum drawdown belong to Series XIX-B — keep XIX-A answers anchored to PPM exposure limits, leverage policy, and general risk factors.
